slides.heading: Avoiding Infinite Loops
slides.body: Avoiding Infinite Loops is part of Indefinite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Avoiding Infinite Loops
slides.body: An infinite loop happens when a loop condition never becomes False. Updating variables correctly helps prevent this problem.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: An infinite loop is like a doorbell stuck ringing because nobody turns it off.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Every while loop needs a condition that can eventually become False, unless you intentionally stop it with break.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Fix a loop by increasing attempts inside the while block.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Write a safe while loop that prints Safe exactly three times.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
